report:
## Conclusion

**The claim is well-supported by research.** Opening a bedroom window improves sleep quality primarily by reducing indoor carbon dioxide (CO₂) levels and regulating temperature. However, opening the bedroom door alone appears less effective.

### Key Evidence

A study from the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) found that opening a bedroom window significantly improved air quality and sleep. When ventilation kept CO₂ below 750 ppm, sleep quality was unaffected by air quality; at higher CO₂ levels, sleep degraded. In the study, 87% of participants reported sleeping soundly with the window open versus 70% with it closed. Notably, opening the bedroom **door** alone did not improve air quality enough to benefit sleep ([DTU News](https://www.dtu.dk/english/newsarchive/2023/05/ventilate-your-bedroom-at-night-you-perform-better-the-next-day)).

A broader review of multiple studies confirmed that inadequate bedroom ventilation consistently disturbs sleep, and that currently prescribed minimum residential ventilation rates may be insufficient for bedrooms ([Taylor & Francis, 2025](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/23744731.2025.2531317)). A field study in student dormitories found that reducing bedroom CO₂ from ~2,500 ppm to under 800 ppm via window opening or fans improved objectively measured sleep quality and next-day cognitive performance ([The Longevity Store summary](https://thelongevitystore.com/blogs/blog/the-ideal-sleep-environment-temperature-light-sound-and-air-quality)).

Additionally, open windows help regulate bedroom temperature toward the ideal sleeping range of approximately 18°C (65°F), preventing overheating that disrupts sleep ([Health Digest](https://www.healthdigest.com/406964/what-happens-to-your-body-when-you-sleep-with-your-window-open/)).

### Caveats
Benefits depend on outdoor air quality, noise, and temperature. In polluted or noisy areas, mechanical ventilation or air purifiers may be preferable. The door-only approach is less effective than window opening for improving sleep.
